name: MathlibAnnex.Analysis.CStarAlgebra.NonUnitalCStarRepresentation.exists_preimage_of_compact_singleton
title: Compact operators lie in a singleton representation range

content.display_title: Compact operators lie in a singleton representation range
content.one_sentence_role: Obtains the inclusion of all compact operators in the image of the original algebra.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $A$ be a nonzero complex $C^*$-algebra, with no unit assumed, let $H$ be a separable complex Hilbert space, and let $\pi:A\to\mathcal B(H)$ be a $*$-representation representing the unique unitary-equivalence class of nonzero irreducible $*$-representations of $A$. If $T\in\mathcal B(H)$ is compact, then $$\exists a\in A,\qquad \pi(a)=T.$$ Thus $\mathcal K(H)\subseteq\pi(A)$.
content.assumptions: Separability is assumed for $H$, not for $A$. The singleton hypothesis includes nonzero irreducibility of $\pi$ and the universal unitary-equivalence condition. Faithfulness is not an input to this theorem.
content.conclusion: The preimage belongs to $A$ itself. The reverse inclusion $\pi(A)\subseteq\mathcal K(H)$ is a separate result.
content.proof_summary: Use faithfulness to close the range, put every rank-one operator in it, and approximate an arbitrary compact operator by finite sums of rank-one operators.
proof_steps: Use the inner product linear in its second argument. Apply [Faithfulness of a non-unital singleton model](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/NonUnital/Singleton.lean#L34-L94) to this nonzero ordered $A$ and this singleton model $\pi$ to obtain injectivity. An injective $C^*$-homomorphism is isometric, so completeness of $A$ makes $\pi(A)$ norm closed. Apply [Every rank-one operator has a preimage](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/NonUnital/CompactRange.lean#L94-L105) to the same $\pi$, using separability of $H$, to obtain preimages of every operator $\theta_{x,y}(z)=\langle y,z\rangle x$. Additivity then supplies preimages of their finite sums.

Here is the compact approximation in [Compact approximation inside the closed representation range](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/NonUnital/CompactRange.lean#L121-L209). For $\varepsilon>0$, the set $K=\overline{T(\overline B_H(0,1))}$ is compact, so choose a finite $\varepsilon/2$-net $N$ for it. Let $E=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}N$ and let $P_E$ be its orthogonal projection. Since $E$ is finite dimensional, $P_E$ exists and minimizes distance to $E$. For $\|z\|\le1$, choose $n\in N$ with $\|Tz-n\|<\varepsilon/2$; then $$\|Tz-P_ETz\|\le\|Tz-n\|<\varepsilon/2.$$ Taking the operator norm gives $\|T-P_ET\|\le\varepsilon/2<\varepsilon$.

Choose an orthonormal basis $e_1,\ldots,e_m$ of $E$. By the inner-product convention just fixed, $$P_ET(z)=\sum_{j=1}^m\langle e_j,Tz\rangle e_j=\sum_{j=1}^m\langle T^*e_j,z\rangle e_j=\sum_{j=1}^m\theta_{e_j,T^*e_j}(z).$$ Step 1 puts this finite sum in $\pi(A)$; the empty sum when $E=0$ is also allowed. Arbitrarily close such approximants place $T$ in the closure of $\pi(A)$, which equals $\pi(A)$. Unpacking membership gives the required $a$.
